sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioners seeking anticipatory bail in the event of their arrest by the respondent - Police in Crime No.02/2024 dated 01.01.2024 registered by Kalaburagi City CEN Crime P.S. for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 465, 468 and 471 r/w Section 149 of Indian Penal Code.

The petitioners are accused Nos.2 to 7.
2.
The factual matrix of the prosecution case are that, on 12.01.2021 one Nazir Ahmed came to complainant's Dall Mill along with two persons and introduced to the complainant.

The accused No.1 in this case informed the complainant that in Sy.No.78/1, there is a commercial land measuring 01 acre 26 guntas and it is owned by him as he purchased the same from accused No.6 for a valuable sale consideration of Rs.6 Crore and 50 lakh and he was able to arrange only Rs.2 Crore 50 lakh and offered the complainant to be partner for the rest of the amount and assured to give him 60% share in plots to NC: 2024:KHC-K:3288 be laid in the said land.
On 20.01.2021 accused No.1 and one Mashak Patel visited the Dall Mill of the complainant, gave documents pertaining to above said land.
On 05.03.2021, the complainant went to the land in which survey was going on.
Thereafter, on 16.06.2021, complainant in the presence of Siddaling Patil and Bhimashankar gave cash of Rs.1 Crore 50 Lakhs and further on 10.10.2021 gave cash of Rs.2 Crore to accused No.1.

However,
accused No.1 insisted to pay Rs.50 Lakh to the land owner i.e., Accused No.6 and also told that if that amount is transferred to his account, he will make him be present at Sub-Registrar office.

Hence, on 18.10.2021, Rs.40 lakh was transferred by the complainant through RTGS to accused No.1.
3.
Later, on 20.12.2021 the property was registered in the name of complainant.
However, the complainant did not receive the sale deed on the date of registration and subsequently on 21.12.2021, he received the sale deed.

After the sale transaction, when the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3288 complainant visited the Sub-Registrar's office and checked the status of the land and sale deed, he was surprised to see that there is no record available in his name in respect of the said property.
Thereafter, he visited to Thasildar's office on 30.12.2023 and came to know that the land in Sy.No.78 belongs to City Corporation, Kalaburagi and there is no Sy.No.78/1.
Hence, he lodged a complaint against the accused No.1 and these petitioners and on the basis of the same a case in Crime No.2/2024 came to be registered.

After registration of FIR, since the respondent- Police making hectic attempt to arrest the petitioners, they approached the I Addl. Dist. & Sessions Judge at Kalaburagi in Crl.Misc.No.538/2024 for grant of anticipatory bail, the same has been rejected by the said court vide order dated 23.04.2024.

entities.text: I Addl. Dist. & Sessions Judge at Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hence, petitioners are before this court for grant of anticipatory bail.

4. I have heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and also learned High Court Government NC:
2024:KHC-K:3288 Pleader for the respondent-State and perused the material available on record.
5.

The primary contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners is that on perusal of the complaint, it is very clear these petitioners are nothing to do with the alleged sale transaction took place between the complainant and the accused No.1.
It is the specific case of the prosecution that accused No.1 had received Rs.3 Croers 60 Lakh from the complainant.

The only allegation against Shivanand And Ors vs The State on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126986034/
3

sentences.text: these petitioners are that accused No.1 has assured that petitioner No.5 is the owner of the said land.

To that effect, the learned counsel places reliance on the order passed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this court in W.P.No.201714/2022 wherein this court directed the Thasildar to mutate the name of father of petitioner No.5 in connection to the land in question.
Hence, according to the learned counsel, the petitioners are in no way indulged in any such activities as alleged in the complaint.
Hence, he prays to allow the petition.

Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the respondent-State opposed the bail petition on the ground that these petitioners were colluded with accused No.1, cheated the complainant to the tune of Rs.2 Crore 60 lakhs, as such, the petitioners do not deserve for grant of anticipatory bail and accordingly prays to reject the bail petition.

7. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the State and having perused the records, it could be seen that the allegation against these petitioners that they are the mediators, in respect of the sale transaction held between accused No.1 and complainant.

As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the petitioners, the Co-ordinate Bench of this court in W.P.No.201714/2022 directed the Thasildar to mutate the name of the petitioner No.5 in the mutation register, as his ownership proved.
Admittedly, the amount in question is received by accused No.1.
Therefore, the petitioners NC: 2024:KHC-K:3288 are nothing to do with the alleged allegations made by the complainant as their role is only as a Mediator between the complainant and the accused No.1.
Therefore, I am of the view that the custodial detention of the petitioners does not called for Further, accused No.1 is already arrested and released on bail.
8. In that view of the matter, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, in my considered view this petitioners may be admitted on anticipatory bail.

Hence, the following:
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., is allowed.

Consequently, the petitioners are directed to be released on anticipatory bail in the event of their arrest by respondent-Police in connection with Crime No.02/2024 dated 01.01.2024 registered by Kalaburagi City CEN Crime P.S. for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 465, 468 and 471 r/w Section 149 of Indian Penal Code NC: 2024:KHC-K:3288 pending on the file of I Addl.

Civil Judge and JMFC, Gulbarga, subject to the following conditions:
i) The petitioners/accused Nos.2 to 7 shall execute personal bond for a sum of `50,000/- each with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer;
